research.policy: Direct Three.js and glTF facts define property contracts. Per-material numbers are bounded starting priors and must be fitted against admitted image evidence and controlled renders.

visualCues: pores and wrinkles at micro scale
limitations: MeshPhysicalMaterial has no true multilayer skin subsurface scattering

visualCues: elongated highlights follow strand or clump direction
limitations: Use geometry clumps or cards for silhouette; a normal map cannot replace hair volume

visualCues: one broad highlight band running across the mass, not per-strand speculars
facet edges read as clump boundaries
limitations: No maps by construction: this pipeline emits code, so anisotropyMap and normalMap are unavailable and every value here has to carry the whole strand impression on its own.

Priors are pushed above hair.human deliberately: on the reference scan the hair surface is smooth (radial roughness 0.00338 against a torso control of 0.00312) and its entire strand appearance lives in the diffuse and normal textures. Without those textures, sheen and anisotropy are the only remaining carriers.
Not calibrated against a reference render. No multipart GLB with separated hair geometry exists to fit these against, so they are a documented starting point and not a measurement.

sheenColor.note: REQUIRED whenever sheen > 0: three's default sheenColor is 0x000000 and the sheen term is a multiply by that colour, so sheen alone contributes exactly zero (WebGLMaterials.js:408). Warm off-white because a hair highlight carries the light's tint, not the hair's.

clearcoatRoughness.note: The low bound is three's own floor: max(clearcoatRoughness, 0.0525) at lights_physical_fragment.glsl.js:72. A smaller number renders as exactly 0.0525.

visualCues: broad soft highlight that moves with the light, not a tight specular dot
tone varies by region: forehead lighter, cheek warmer, jaw cooler
limitations: No maps by construction: this pipeline emits code, so map/roughnessMap/normalMap are unavailable and the whole skin impression rests on base colour, clearcoat and per-region tone.

MeshPhysicalMaterial has no true multilayer subsurface scattering, and transmission is NOT a substitute -- it is a screen-space refraction (glass) model that on a closed body mesh renders a glassy figure and costs an extra render target. transmission/thickness are therefore forbidden on this family.

clearcoatRoughness has geometryRoughness ADDED at shade time (lights_physical_fragment.glsl.js:73), so a value tuned on smooth geometry reads blurrier flat-shaded. Author it on the final tessellation.
Not calibrated against a reference render. These are a documented starting point, not a measurement.

sheenRoughness.note: High for cotton/linen/wool: a broad soft rim. Drop toward 0.2 only for a visible satin rim, and never on sparse geometry where a tight rim lands on a few facets and reads as plastic.

visualCues: diffuse body with a grazing-angle rim
folds and hems read as geometry, never as texture
limitations: No maps by construction, so sheen is the entire woven cue available.

Enabling sheen DARKENS this material's own diffuse base by 0.157 x effective sheen strength (sheenEnergyComp, meshphysical.glsl.js:205). Author the base colour brighter by 1/(1-darkening) or the render lands darker than the reference at every non-grazing angle.
Large folds and hems belong in geometry, per fabric.woven-matte. A code-only profile cannot fake them with a normal map.
A garment shell with an open hem, cuff or collar must set side to DoubleSide; three defaults to FrontSide and culls the backfaces, so the opening renders as a hole.
Not calibrated against a reference render.

sheenColor.note: REQUIRED whenever sheen > 0. sheen and sheenColor are multiplied into ONE uniform before upload (WebGLMaterials.js:408), so they are a single degree of freedom -- extract the tint, keep sheen as an authored strength.

limitations: Geometry shells, tufts or cards are required for identity-scale fur
Large folds and hems belong in geometry
Highlight direction must follow the authored fibre tangent

visualCues: strong soft rim or grazing sheen
limitations: Short pile is an approximation without a fibre shader
Single images rarely prove natural versus synthetic leather
A meaningful environment map is mandatory; flat lighting cannot validate polished metal
Anisotropy direction must agree with geometry tangent and visible brushing
Steel versus aluminium may require context or metadata

visualCues: patina may create rough dielectric corrosion regions
limitations: Patina and oxidation require region masks rather than one uniform metal recipe
Brass versus bronze versus gold may require context or metadata

visualCues: yellow conductor reflection rather than yellow diffuse paint
limitations: Gold identity should not be inferred from yellow albedo alone

visualCues: diffuse paint colour under a separate glossy coat
limitations: Intact paint is dielectric; exposed substrate needs a separate region or mask

visualCues: untinted or light-coloured specular over coloured diffuse body
limitations: Do not set metalness from highlight sharpness alone
Context and texture frequency often distinguish matte plastics from rubber
Wet or polished rubber needs a separate finish record
Species identity cannot usually be established from a small crop

visualCues: wood grain under a separate glossy layer
limitations: Do not bake the coating highlight into the grain albedo
Marble and polished stone may need transmission or subsurface approximation beyond this base record
Unglazed ceramic needs a separate matte finish
Use opacity 1 with transmission; thickness must be derived from geometry scale
Transmission quality and cost depend on renderer and scene configuration
A painted opaque gem-like surface is not a transmissive gemstone and needs a coating record
